description: Renovate runs as the GitHub App on this account, not as a self-hosted workflow. That is what makes its commits signed: an App installation token creates them through the API and GitHub signs them with its web-flow key, which verify-pr-signatures requires. A PAT gets attribution but no signature.

This file used to restate the shared jdwlabs preset key for key -- same schedule, limits, labels and vulnerability handling -- which is the drift a preset exists to prevent. It extends it now, and keeps only what is true of this repository: the Bedrock protocol library and the Go toolchain both need a human.
Batch all non-major updates into a single weekly PR per repo to keep noise reviewable

Automerged. Merging here neither releases nor deploys: release.yml fires on a v* tag rather than on push, and this image is enabled:false in jdw-deployments' Renovate config, so the tag the cluster runs only ever moves by hand. A merged update changes the default branch and nothing else -- which is what makes automerge safe here and not in jdw-deployments. The required checks still gate it, and majors are not in this group.
gophertunnel carries the Bedrock packet schema this binary speaks, so an upgrade can change which server versions the bot can reach at all.

Reviewed on its own rather than inside the weekly batch, and not gated to the weekly window: the protocol-check CronJob reports when production has moved past what this binary speaks, and the fix is whatever gophertunnel release supports it.
Never automerged, for the same reason it is ungrouped: this is the one dependency where a green build does not mean the bot can still reach the server.
The Go toolchain in the build stage must not run ahead of the `go` directive in go.mod, which is what CI and local builds are pinned to.
Raise this in the same change that raises go.mod, so a toolchain the module has not been tested against never reaches the image alone.
Ungrouped, so it is never automerged: it takes the go.mod change with it, which is a review.
